config_sensitivity.note: Returns are extremely lumpy: across 4 twelve-month periods the account ran from -24 to +32 points against the index. Any single window's CAGR is mostly a statement about which years it contains, so the period table below matters more than the headline. 30 defensible book structures (40-100 positions, 5-9% total risk) run over the held-out window. Median 6.50% a year, 5.8% to 7.0% across the middle half. Pre-split ranking carried a rank correlation of -0.05 with held-out return, which is too weak to select on.

health.note: Over 11 switches, invested days returned +0.026% against -0.046% out — a gap of +0.072pp. The rule is still discriminating, at 53% exposure against 72% in the study.

regime_timing.method: Hold the Nifty 500 while the regime is bull_strong, bull_narrow or recovery; park cash otherwise. The regime set was chosen on 2007-2017 from five candidates declared in advance, scored on return per unit of drawdown, and the second half was run once. Cash earns a real rate, switches cost 5 bps, and tax is charged on every realised gain at the short-term rate where the holding lasted under a year.
regime_timing.caveat: This is index timing, not stock selection — the selection side of this system has no edge at all. The drawdown advantage comes from being out of the market for roughly 40% of the time, including stretches when it is rising, which is the part a person finds hardest to actually do.

comparisons.verdict: The account's 7.6% CAGR is below 79% of 701 professionally managed funds, but loses to Nifty 500 buy-and-hold (9.9%), which needed no work at all, with a shallower worst drawdown (-19% against a fund median of -27%).

uncertainty.note: 1,686 trades drawn from 42,811 eligible signals. Resampling that pool to the same count puts 90% of outcomes between 11.8% and 24.0% a year, with a median of 17.6% — against a realised 7.6%. The width is what 1,686 draws from a right-skewed distribution buys you, and any gap below the median is the cost of only being able to enter when capacity frees up, which happens fastest after a loss.

uncertainty.note: 1,686 trades drawn from 42,811 eligible signals. Resampling that pool to the same count puts 90% of outcomes between 11.8% and 24.0% a year, with a median of 17.6% — against a realised 7.6%. The width is what 1,686 draws from a right-skewed distribution buys you, and any gap below the median is the cost of only being able to enter when capacity frees up, which happens fastest after a loss.

answer.summary: Measured over 3 years it never saw, against 701 real funds: better on 3 of 6 measures, level on 1, worse on 2. Only 115 of them (16.4%) beat it on return and drawdown at the same time — the comparison with no axis left to pick. On Sharpe, which is how professional performance is actually judged, it sits at the 89th percentile. It earns less than the median fund in raw return, and does so taking roughly half the drawdown.

caveats: Fund returns are realised money; the bot's are simulated. A simulation never hesitates, never oversleeps, and never sizes down after three losses in a row.
Funds must stay invested under their mandate. The bot is allowed to sit in cash, which is a large structural advantage in a falling market and is not skill.
Fund NAV is net of every real cost including the manager's fee. The bot's costs are modelled (STT, stamp duty, exchange, GST, 15 bps slippage), not incurred.
The bot's universe is today's listed companies, so it never traded anything that went to zero. The funds did.

The held-out window is under four years and R outcomes are heavily right-skewed, so the CAGR for it is one draw from a wide distribution rather than a measurement — see the uncertainty block for the range the same edge could have produced.
benchmark.method: The bot's trade record is run as an actual account — finite capital, eight concurrent positions, risk-based sizing — taking only strategies that were confirmed at the time, never with hindsight. The resulting CAGR is then placed inside the distribution of real Indian equity funds over a matching window, and against Nifty buy-and-hold.

status_catalogue.label: Candidate
status_catalogue.note: Looks positive but has not traded enough to be trusted yet.

status_catalogue.label: Rejected
status_catalogue.note: No edge over the sample available.

verdict_catalogue.label: Clean win
verdict_catalogue.note: Never in serious trouble and kept most of the move. This is the shape the system is built to produce.

verdict_catalogue.label: Won, gave back most of it
verdict_catalogue.note: Profitable, but most of the best excursion was surrendered on the way out. A structural leak if it is common.

verdict_catalogue.label: Won after nearly stopping out
verdict_catalogue.note: Came within a fraction of the stop before working. Won, but the decision was closer to wrong than the result suggests.

verdict_catalogue.label: Was well in profit, lost it all
verdict_catalogue.note: The worst shape in the book: a real profit handed back in full. Not a market problem — an exit problem.

verdict_catalogue.label: Clean loss — wrong fast, cheap
verdict_catalogue.note: Wrong quickly and cheaply. Nothing to fix; this is what the stop is for.

verdict_catalogue.label: Went nowhere, timed out
verdict_catalogue.note: Never moved either way and died of old age. Costs little but occupies capital and attention.

verdict_catalogue.label: Gapped through the stop
verdict_catalogue.note: Opened through the stop. Unavoidable and the reason position size, not the stop, is the real risk control.

learning.method_note: Cell standing is re-scored quarterly using only trades that had closed by that date, so the timeline shows what the system actually believed at each point — including where it was wrong and later stood a strategy down. Nothing is refitted: a cell that stops paying is retired, not repaired.

strategy_catalogue.label: Minervini Breakout
strategy_catalogue.thesis: A stage-2 leader clearing a 20-day high on expanding volume.

strategy_catalogue.label: VCP Breakout
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Volatility contracts to a coil inside an uptrend, then price breaks out of it.

strategy_catalogue.label: 52-Week High Breakout
strategy_catalogue.thesis: New yearly high on volume — the crudest and most-studied momentum edge.

strategy_catalogue.label: Momentum Burst
strategy_catalogue.thesis: A sharp thrust out of a quiet stretch; rides short-horizon continuation.

strategy_catalogue.label: High Tight Flag
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Doubled in a quarter, then consolidated without giving much back.

strategy_catalogue.label: Pullback to 21 EMA
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Buys the first orderly pullback in an established uptrend.

strategy_catalogue.label: Pullback to 50 DMA
strategy_catalogue.thesis: The deeper reset — a full pullback to the 50 DMA that holds.

strategy_catalogue.label: Oversold Bounce
strategy_catalogue.thesis: RSI washout while the long-term trend is intact. Predicted to pay in pullbacks and chop, and to be a trap in a genuine bear.

strategy_catalogue.label: Volatility Squeeze
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Range compresses to a multi-month low, then resolves. No directional prior about the index — the control case for regime dependence.

strategy_catalogue.label: Gap Continuation
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Gaps out of a base on heavy volume and holds the gap into the close.

strategy_catalogue.label: Earnings Drift
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Inside the drift window after a large positive earnings surprise, with price confirming. Tests whether a different kind of information carries an edge the price patterns do not.

strategy_catalogue.label: Earnings Gap Hold
strategy_catalogue.thesis: A positive surprise that gapped, held the gap, and is still inside its drift window. Unlike the plain gap setup, this one knows why the stock gapped.

strategy_catalogue.label: Pocket Pivot
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Morales & Kacher: an up day inside a base whose volume beats every down day of the prior ten — accumulation before the breakout.

strategy_catalogue.label: NR7 Release
strategy_catalogue.thesis: Crabel: the narrowest range of seven sessions, then its high gives way.

strategy_catalogue.label: Results Follow-Through
strategy_catalogue.thesis: A results-day breakaway gap that consolidates, then clears its 20-day closing high.

strategy_catalogue.label: Episodic Pivot
strategy_catalogue.thesis: A 6%+ gap on triple volume out of a dormant stretch — new information being priced.

regime_catalogue.label: Strong Bull
regime_catalogue.note: Index above a rising 200 DMA with the majority of stocks participating.

regime_catalogue.label: Narrow Bull
regime_catalogue.note: Index still holding its 200 DMA, but breadth has rolled over — fewer names carrying it.

regime_catalogue.label: Choppy / Rangebound
regime_catalogue.note: No trend. Price keeps crossing back and forth through the 50 DMA.

regime_catalogue.label: Correction
regime_catalogue.note: A defined pullback from the highs, inside what is still a longer uptrend.

regime_catalogue.label: Bear
regime_catalogue.note: Below a falling 200 DMA and well off the highs.

regime_catalogue.label: Recovery
regime_catalogue.note: Reclaiming after a decline, before the long-term trend has turned back up.
